shower.thought: # Shower Thoughts
We're all just trying to get good enough at life to not die, but the moment we think we've figured it out, the rules change.
The people who hurt you the most are usually the ones who reminded you that you were capable of being hurt at all.
You've never actually seen your own face—only reflections and photos of someone pretending to be you.
Silence isn't the absence of sound; it's just noise you've learned to stop hearing.
The worst part about growing up is realizing your parents were improvising the whole time.
Every time you learn how something works, it becomes slightly less magical.
Your biggest weakness is probably something you've never named.
We spend so much time preparing for the future that we miss the only moment we can actually do anything in.
The people you can't stop thinking about are usually people you can't do anything about.
You're more afraid of being truly known than you are of being alone.
Most of your decisions aren't made by you—they're made by whoever you were trying to impress five years ago.
Time moves faster the less you're paying attention to it, which might be why childhood lasts forever and adulthood disappears.
The things you regret most are usually the risks you didn't take, not the ones you did.
You can't actually imagine a new color, which means your mind has a ceiling you can't see.
People don't change because they see the truth—they change because they get tired.
The real test of your character isn't what you do when everything's okay; it's what you do when the outcome doesn't matter to anyone but you.
You're nostalgic for times you didn't fully appreciate when they were happening, which means you're probably wasting the present too.
Every conversation you have is a negotiation between two incomplete versions of the truth.
The moment you admit you were wrong, you become smarter than you were before.

motivational.thought: The person you're becoming is already cheering for the person you are right now. — Unknown
Discipline is just choosing between what you want now and what you want most. — Unknown
Your life doesn't improve by chance, it improves by change. — Ralph Marston
The greatest tragedy is not failure. It's the years spent afraid to try. — Unknown
You are not behind. You are exactly where you need to be to become who you're meant to be. — Unknown
What looks like luck from the outside is usually just preparation meeting opportunity on the inside. — Unknown
The only person you're destined to become is the one you decide to be. — Ralph Waldo Emerson
Every setback is just a setup for a comeback you won't see coming. — Unknown
You don't rise to the level of your goals. You fall to the level of your systems. — Unknown
Healing isn't linear, and neither is growth. Both are still progress. — Unknown
The version of you that exists six months from now is being shaped by what you choose today. — Unknown
Hard work without direction is just exhaustion. But direction without hard work is just a dream. — Unknown
You've survived 100% of your worst days. That's a perfect track record. — Unknown
Comfort is the enemy of growth, but panic is too. The magic is in the stretch. — Unknown
Your future self is watching you right now. Make them proud. — Unknown
The difference between who you are and who you want to be is what you do. — Bill Phillips
Regret for things we did can be tempered by time; regret for things we did not do is inconsolable. — Sydney Smith
Success is the sum of small efforts repeated day in and day out. — Robert Collier
You are allowed to be both a masterpiece and a work in progress simultaneously. — Sophia Bush
The world breaks everyone, and afterward, some are strong at the broken places. — Ernest Hemingway

darkjoke.thought:
I told my wife she was being dramatic about her birthday.
Apparently "another year closer to death" isn't the compliment I thought it was.
I have a stepladder because my real ladder left when I was just a kid.

My grandfather said, "Your generation is too reliant on technology."
I said, "OK boomer," and he had a stroke.

I love the sound of children laughing in the morning.
It's the one time I know exactly where they are.

My therapist asked if I had any suicidal thoughts.
I said, "Not yet, but give me time—you're charging $300 an hour."

I went to a seafood restaurant and ordered lobster.
The waiter said, "It's a living."
It wasn't anymore.

People keep asking me why I'm so good at funerals.
I keep things light—unlike the deceased.

My dentist told me I need to floss more.
I said, "You need to stop judging people while your hands are in their mouth."
He said, "Fair point, but you still have cavities."

I asked my dad why he named me after the sound a dying animal makes.
He said, "You'll understand when you're older."
I'm 35. Still waiting.

I told my friend his baby looked just like him.
He seemed happy until the paternity test.

My wife accused me of never listening to her.
At least I think that's what she said—I wasn't really paying attention.

I'm reading a book on the history of glue.
I can't put it down, and honestly, my therapist says I shouldn't try.

My dad's ashes are kept in an urn on the mantle.
My mom says he always wanted to watch over the family.
Personally, I think he's just trying to spy on my dating life.

I went to a self-help seminar about overcoming perfectionism.
The instructor kept making small mistakes and it ruined the whole experience.

My kid asked, "Dad, are you listening to me?"
I said, "Of course," without looking up from my phone.
He's apparently been missing for three days.

I told my date I was a doctor.
When she found out I meant philosophy, she got upset.
I said, "Well, I'm sick of it too."
The worst time to realize you have a fear of heights is during the divorce proceedings.

My therapist asked what my biggest regret was.
I said, "Probably naming my son Regret."
He's not coming home for Christmas.

People say money can't buy happiness.
But it can buy a jet ski.
Have you ever seen someone frown on a jet ski?
I have—the coast guard is very serious about regulations.

I told my girlfriend she had beautiful eyes.
Turns out they were a gift from her organ donor.
The wedding is off.
